list: the official 55 trophies, 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze, 28 hidden
note: Names, descriptions and grades are the official list as published by the guides below. Every guide step is written fresh for this entry, in its own words, and names the guide it draws on. GTA VI released 19 Nov 2026 (PowerPyx); early-guide details may change as players confirm them in game, and this guide says so where it matters.

disputes.title: Is the Chapter 1 meditation required?
disputes.a: PowerPyx: the first meditation (Lucia on the balcony at Jason's house, after the mission Down to Earth) raises the counter by 1 but is not marked as a Meditation Spot like the rest, so it is currently unclear whether it is required.
disputes.b: GTABase and EGamers flag Positive Mental Attitude as the list's only possibly missable trophy and say to do the Chapter 1 meditation anyway, because it disappears once Chapter 1 ends.
disputes.verdict: Do it in Chapter 1. It costs a minute, and skipping it risks a full second playthrough.

disputes.title: How long is the platinum, really?
disputes.a: PowerPyx rates the set 4/10 and puts the platinum at roughly 200 hours, with the story at 60-80 hours.
disputes.b: Push Square says to expect 300 hours or more to see and do almost everything.
disputes.verdict: Plan for 200 hours of guided play; the extra 100 in the higher estimate is unhurried exploring, not extra requirements.

disputes.title: How much of the game is 100% completion?
disputes.a: PowerPyx: the 100% Completion Checklist is closer to 60% true completion — most side quests are not required and collectibles are only partly required.
disputes.b: Push Square: the checklist still asks for 15 of the 18 Collectible Card sets, and PowerPyx itself lists 200 of 277 vehicles to scan and 100 of 255 animals to study.
disputes.verdict: Both agree the checklist is lenient. Follow the checklist itself after the story, not a 100%-of-everything run.

disputes.title: Cunning Stunts: do repeats count?
disputes.a: KeenGamer describes the trophy as 250 unique stunts.
disputes.b: Push Square counts 397 stunts in the game and says you need a little over half of them, which reads as 250 completed stunts rather than 250 different ones.
disputes.verdict: Play it safe: do 250 different stunts. Different ones satisfy both readings.

disputes.title: Whip It Good: scan or drive?
disputes.a: GTABase (as reported by EGamers): you scan 100 different vehicles with WAiNK, with no need to drive them; scanning traffic near busy roads is efficient.
disputes.b: Vice City Hustle and the trophy wording say discover 100 vehicles, and the 100% checklist separately asks you to scan 200 of 277 base models — so the trophy's 100 may be the same scanning action, or a broader discover count.
disputes.verdict: Scan every new vehicle you see with WAiNK. Scanning satisfies the stricter reading and feeds the 100% checklist too.

disputes.title: How many trophies can actually be missed?
disputes.a: PowerPyx and GTABase: potentially 1 — Positive Mental Attitude, and only the Chapter 1 meditation.
disputes.b: TechWiser (as reported by EGamers): the Stranger mission chains behind five hidden trophies have windows tied to story progress.
disputes.verdict: One confirmed risk, five to watch. PowerPyx adds that all trophy-related quest givers return in free-roam, so the stranger chains are a watch item, not a confirmed miss — but do them as they appear.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum pops on its own the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned. There is no extra task, no final challenge and no separate unlock — it is a receipt, not a job.

steps.t: Earn the other 54 trophies in any order; the platinum unlocks automatically with the last one.
If it does not pop, open Touch Pad, then Progress, and check which trophy is still open — Push Square's tracking note is that the Progress menu shows what is left.
No online play is needed: all 55 trophies are offline and single-player, so the platinum needs no co-op partner or server.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: The opening mission, Gone Fishing, is the first thing you play. Finish it and the trophy is yours — it cannot be missed, skipped or failed permanently.

steps.t: Play the opening mission Gone Fishing through to its end; it is the game's first mission, not an optional one.
If a mission step stalls, follow the on-screen objective marker — story missions in this guide's sources are all linear and unmissable.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 1. The story is split into 5 chapters (PowerPyx), so this is the first of five chapter trophies, and it unlocks the moment the chapter's last mission ends.

steps.t: Play through Chapter 1's missions in order until the chapter closes.
Before the chapter ends, do the Chapter 1 meditation at Jason's house — see Positive Mental Attitude. It is the one thing in Chapter 1 that may not come back.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 2. Like the other chapter trophies it is unmissable story progress — play the chapter through and it pops at the end.

steps.t: Play through Chapter 2's missions in order until the chapter closes.
Use the chapter to start side habits that pay off later: scan new vehicles with WAiNK and try the activities you pass, since progress made during the story already counts toward the 100% checklist.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 3. By now Vice City itself is open to you, so this is also the natural point to start the Vice City activities — bowling, the arcade and the drone races — between missions.

steps.t: Play through Chapter 3's missions in order until the chapter closes.
Between missions, try the Vice City activities once each — they feed Master of None and cost nothing to sample.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 4. Four of the five chapters are now done; the remaining story trophy after this one is the final mission itself.

steps.t: Play through Chapter 4's missions in order until the chapter closes.
Before the finale, clear any stranger strands that are open — PowerPyx notes all trophy-related quest givers return in free-roam, but doing them now keeps the endgame short.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Finish the final story mission. This is the gold story trophy and the doorway to the endgame: after it, free-roam stays open, the 100% Completion Checklist becomes viewable, and everything needed for it is still reachable.

steps.t: Play the final mission to its end; the trophy pops with the credits, not with a side objective.
After the story, open Touch Pad, then Progress, then 100% Completion — Push Square's note is that the checklist only becomes viewable once the story is done.
Do not worry about mission replay: there is none, and PowerPyx confirms free-roam continues after the story with nothing trophy-related locked away.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run. It is a named mission trophy, so it pops when that mission's objectives are done — no extra condition hides behind it.

steps.t: Take the Breakfast Run mission when it appears in the story and play it through.
Story missions cannot be missed; if the mission is not offered yet, keep playing the chapter — it unlocks in sequence.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. Treat it as a rehearsal for the free-roam heist trophies (bank vaults, armored trucks): the same habits — plan the escape route before you start — apply there.

steps.t: Take The Cartel Heist when the story offers it and play it through.
Note how the heist escape works; Maximum Withdrawal and A Classic Blitz Play later ask for the same thing in free-roam — rob, then escape.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play. A straight story trophy: the mission appears in sequence, you finish it, the trophy pops.

steps.t: Take the Child's Play mission when it appears and play it through.
No side requirement is attached to it in any published list — the mission itself is the whole condition.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. Another mission trophy with no hidden condition — finish the mission and move on.

steps.t: Take the Headliners mission when the story offers it and play it through.
If you are tracking the platinum, this is one of twelve story trophies that need no extra work at all.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown, set at Vice City International Airport. Learn the airport's layout here — the free-roam trophy Catch Me If You Can later asks you to leave the same airport in an unscheduled way.

steps.t: Take the VCIA Takedown mission when the story offers it and play it through.
Remember the airport exits and runway layout from this mission; they are the same ground Catch Me If You Can uses.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. The last of the named-mission story trophies — after this, the remaining story trophies are the chapters and the finale.

steps.t: Take the Operation Savage Glory mission when the story offers it and play it through.
With the mission trophies done, the story's remaining trophies are chapter completions and the final mission.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% on the in-game Completion Checklist. This is the hardest trophy in the set (PowerPyx, EGamers) — but the checklist is lenient: it asks for roughly 60% of true completion, most side quests are not required, and collectibles are only partly required.

steps.t: Finish the story first: the checklist only becomes viewable after the final mission, though progress made during the story already counts toward it.
Open the checklist at Touch Pad, then Progress, then 100% Completion, and work down it — it is the authoritative list of what is left.
Expect the checklist to ask for 15 of the 18 Collectible Card sets, per Push Square — not all 18.
Expect vehicle and animal targets of 200 of 277 base-model vehicles scanned and 100 of 255 animals studied through binoculars, per PowerPyx.
Do not chase 100% of everything: PowerPyx's whole point is that the checklist is closer to 60% true completion, so stop at what the checklist itself asks for.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts across Leonida. Stunts are the game's jump, base-jump and precision-driving challenges; there are 397 in the game (Push Square), so you need a little over half of them.

steps.t: Attempt stunts as you travel — jumps, ramps and base jumps all feed the count, and progress made during the story already counts.
Base jumps: leap off the tallest peaks and buildings, drop through the checkpoints as fast as possible, then parachute onto the target — that is Push Square's description of how they work.
Do 250 different stunts, not 250 repeats: KeenGamer reads the trophy as 250 unique stunts, and different ones satisfy both readings of the requirement.
Track the count in Touch Pad, then Progress, and mop up the remainder in free-roam after the story.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each of the nine activity types at least once (KeenGamer). This is a sampler trophy: one go at everything, not mastery of anything — a single attempt at each type is enough.

steps.t: Try one Shooting Range challenge — the range is also where The Shootist's 42 gold medals live.
Try one race and one Top Fun drone race; both are activity types with their own trophies.
Try fishing, an arcade game and bowling — KeenGamer counts nine types, and these three are named across the guides as activity types.
Try meditation and a stunt as well, then check the count: nine types tried once each is the whole condition.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. This is one of the two hardest trophies in the set (EGamers, GamesFuze): gold on every challenge, at both range locations, with no silver counting toward it.

steps.t: Find the Shooting Range: there are two locations in Leonida, per Push Square.
Work through all 42 challenges — KeenGamer and Push Square agree on the number, and every one of them needs gold.
Replay a challenge until the gold medal lands; a silver or bronze on any single challenge leaves the trophy locked.
Use the range early: range skill carries into the story's gunfights, and the challenges are available long before the endgame.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at all 14 locations (KeenGamer). One win per location — winning the same location twice does not cover another one.

steps.t: Find the Top Fun drone races across Leonida; there are 14 locations to win at.
Win one race at each location, and tick locations off as you go — the counter below tracks 14.
A drone race also counts as one of the nine activity types for Master of None, so do at least one early.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. The word that matters is different: twenty wins on the same circuit do not count — spread the wins across twenty distinct races.

steps.t: Enter races across Leonida and win twenty distinct ones.
Vary the race type and location rather than repeating a favourite — the trophy counts distinct races.
Races are one of the nine activity types, so the first win also feeds Master of None.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Fishing is one of the game's activities, and Cal is the rival angler the challenge is built around — win the head-to-head and the trophy is yours.

steps.t: Take up fishing until the challenge against Cal is offered.
Beat Cal in the fishing challenge itself — the win, not just taking part, is the condition.
Fishing also counts as one of the nine activity types for Master of None.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game, start to finish. Any arcade game counts — pick the shortest one you enjoy and see it through to its end screen.

steps.t: Find an arcade in Leonida and start any arcade game.
Play it through to completion; quitting halfway does not count.
The arcade also counts as one of the nine activity types for Master of None.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Andy's strand. Andy is one of five stranger quest-givers with a hidden final-mission trophy (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone). Do his missions as they appear.

steps.t: Find Andy's missions as they appear across Leonida and work through the strand to its final mission.
If Andy goes quiet for a while, keep playing the story: PowerPyx notes quest givers can become temporarily unavailable and return later, and all trophy-related givers are still there in free-roam.

TechWiser (as reported by EGamers) says stranger chains have windows tied to story progress, so do not leave Andy's strand sitting for whole chapters — this guide lists it as a watch item, not a confirmed miss.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Kenton's strand. Same pattern as Andy's: a stranger's mission chain that ends in one final mission, with the trophy popping when that mission ends.

steps.t: Work through Kenton's missions as they appear until the final one is offered.
If Kenton is temporarily unavailable, keep playing — PowerPyx says trophy-related quest givers become available again later in the game.
Do the strand as it comes rather than banking it for the endgame, because TechWiser reports story-linked windows on stranger chains.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Billy's strand. Billy's chain is one of the five stranger strands with a hidden trophy at its end — finish the chain and the trophy follows.

steps.t: Work through Billy's missions as they appear until the final one is offered.
Quest givers can vanish for stretches of the story and return later, per PowerPyx — a missing Billy is a delay, not a lockout.
Clear the strand before the finale if you can; the watch flag here is TechWiser's report of story-linked windows on stranger chains.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across Leonida. A strand is a whole chain for one stranger, not one mission — eight full chains, finished end to end.

steps.t: Take stranger missions (black icons with pink letters, per PowerPyx) whenever they appear, and follow each chain to its end.
Count full strands, not missions: eight completed chains is the condition, and the five hidden final-mission trophies (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) are five of them.
Optional missions that disappear after a while do not matter for trophies, per PowerPyx — but a strand you are already in is worth finishing while it is open.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Randy's strand. The fourth of the five stranger final-mission trophies — same approach: follow the chain as it appears, finish the last mission.

steps.t: Work through Randy's missions as they appear until the final one is offered.
If Randy is unavailable for a stretch, keep playing the story; PowerPyx notes trophy-related givers return later.
Treat the strand as a watch item: TechWiser reports story-linked windows on stranger chains, so do not park it for whole chapters.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Tyrone's strand. The fifth and last of the stranger final-mission trophies — finish Tyrone's chain and the set of five is complete.

steps.t: Work through Tyrone's missions as they appear until the final one is offered.
A temporarily absent Tyrone is normal mid-story, per PowerPyx; he returns later in the game.
Clear the strand when it is open — the watch flag is TechWiser's report of story-linked windows on stranger chains.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every meditation spot across Leonida — 18 spots in 10 locations, using both Jason and Lucia (Vice City Hustle). This is the list's only possibly missable trophy (PowerPyx, GTABase): the first meditation, in Chapter 1, disappears when the chapter ends.

steps.t: In Chapter 1, after the mission Down to Earth, talk to Lucia in the kitchen in the morning — she says she is going to meditate, then goes to the balcony. Follow her and choose Accept. This is PowerPyx's step-by-step account of the missable meditation.

Do that Chapter 1 meditation even though it is not marked as a Meditation Spot like the rest: PowerPyx says it raises the counter by 1 and it is unclear whether it is required, while GTABase and EGamers say to do it to be safe.
Then meditate at the remaining spots across Leonida — 18 spots in 10 locations, with both Jason and Lucia, per Vice City Hustle.
Check the counter in Touch Pad, then Progress, as you go; the tracker below counts to 18.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret's hunt is a one-off: a single named animal, not a quota of ordinary game — find it, take it down, and the trophy pops.

steps.t: Take Bret's hunt when it is offered and follow his lead to the unique animal.
Studying animals through binoculars feeds the 100% checklist (100 of 255 animals, per PowerPyx), so study wildlife as you travel even though this trophy only needs the one hunt.
Hunting counts as one of the nine activity types for Master of None.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 Collectible Card sets, out of 18 sets in the game (Vice City Hustle, Push Square). Three full sets is the trophy; the 100% checklist separately asks for 15 of the 18, so keep collecting past the trophy.

steps.t: Pick up Collectible Cards as you explore; there are 18 sets in total.
Finish any 3 sets completely — a set only counts when every card in it is found.
Keep going after the trophy: Push Square says the 100% checklist wants 15 full sets, so the trophy is the first fifth of that job.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use WAiNK It at 100 locations. WAiNK It is the in-game scanning app: point it at landmarks, curiosities and sculptures across Leonida and log them, any mix counting toward the 100.

steps.t: Open the WAiNK app and scan points of interest as you travel — any mix of Landmarks (31), Curiosities (35), Sculptures (23) and No Flusher tags counts, per Vice City Hustle.
Scan 100 locations in total; the tracker below counts to 100.
Scanning also feeds Whip It Good (vehicles) and the 100% checklist's 200-vehicle scan target, so scan vehicles too whenever they are new.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges. Challenges are the game's small objectives scattered across activities — finish fifty of them, in any mix, and the trophy pops.

steps.t: Take on challenges as they appear across activities and free-roam; any mix of fifty counts.
Check the count in Touch Pad, then Progress, and mop up the remainder in free-roam after the story.
Challenges overlap with the activity trophies, so a normal playthrough that samples everything will already be well on the way to fifty.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star Wanted Level while playing with your partner, then escape. The two of you build the heat together and lose it together — the escape, not just the wanted level, is the condition.

steps.t: With your partner alongside, raise your Wanted Level to 4 stars.
Break line of sight and escape the search area with your partner still with you — the trophy is for losing the heat together.
Pick open ground with a fast car nearby before you start; the escape is easier planned than improvised.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level. Three in a row, one heat: the wanted level must survive all three robberies, so keep the police close but not catching you.

steps.t: With your partner, rob a first shop and keep your Wanted Level — do not lose the heat between robberies.
Move straight to a second shop, then a third, still with the same Wanted Level running.
Plan the route first: three shops close together, a getaway car ready, and no detours that let the heat cool off.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles. The fastest reading, from GTABase, is to scan them with WAiNK — no need to drive them — and busy roads are the efficient place to find new models.

steps.t: Scan every new vehicle you see with WAiNK It; GTABase (as reported by EGamers) says scanning 100 different vehicles counts, with no need to drive them.
Work busy roads and traffic hotspots, where new models pass constantly — that is GTABase's efficiency tip.
Keep scanning past 100: the 100% checklist asks for 200 of 277 base models scanned, per PowerPyx, so this trophy is halfway there.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus. One activation, five takedowns — the whole condition lives inside one Combat Focus window, so set the scene before you trigger it.

steps.t: Find a fight with at least five enemies grouped together before you trigger Combat Focus.
Activate Combat Focus once, then take down five enemies inside that single use — a second activation starts a new count.
If the group thins out, back off and set up a bigger group rather than spending the activation on two or three.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA — Vice City International Airport. Leave the airport by an exit that is not a scheduled flight: take a plane, or drive out fast, on your own timetable.

steps.t: Go to VCIA, the airport you already know from the Hi-Jacked mission.
Leave by an unscheduled departure — take an aircraft out yourself rather than following a scheduled flight.
The airport layout from the VCIA Takedown mission is the same ground, so use the runways and exits you learned there.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The Rhinos are the game's tanks, and this trophy is about tangling with them. The description itself is the hint — 'Kinda hot in these Rhinos' — so expect a hot, loud encounter with a Rhino tank.

steps.t: Find a Rhino tank in free-roam — the trophy is tied to the Rhinos, not to ordinary vehicles.
Engage with the Rhino as the trophy implies: get into the tank encounter rather than avoiding it.
High wanted levels are the usual way tanks appear in GTA games, so build heat if no Rhino is around — and save first.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. Stealth is the whole condition: get in, take the goods and get out with nobody raising the alarm.

steps.t: Pick a jewelry store and plan a quiet entry — the trophy fails if you are detected, so speed matters less than silence.
Rob the store and leave without triggering an alarm or a wanted response.
If you are spotted, leave and try another store rather than fighting through — detection is what the trophy forbids.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape — five times over. Each vault needs the full loop: break in, take the vault, then escape clean. The escape is part of the count, so a vault you rob but get caught on does not count.

steps.t: Find a bank vault, rob it, and escape — the escape is part of the condition, per the trophy wording as published by every guide.
Repeat for five vaults in total; the tracker below counts to 5.
Plan each escape before you enter, as in the story's Cartel Heist — a getaway car and a route out beat improvising under heat.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. One truck, one clean getaway — the name nods to the classic GTA V heist, but the condition is simple: take the truck's haul and lose the heat.

steps.t: Find an armored truck on the road in free-roam.
Rob it, then escape — as with the bank vaults, the escape is part of the condition.
Have a getaway vehicle ready before you hit the truck; the heat starts the moment the robbery does.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida — all 52 areas, as the PSN count behind the list records (Exophase, PSNProfiles). In practice that means clearing the fog from the whole map.

steps.t: Clear the fog across the whole map of Leonida; Vice City Hustle (as reported by EGamers) says flying over the dark patches is the quickest way.
Cover all 52 areas — the PSN count for this trophy is 52, per Exophase and PSNProfiles.
Use a plane for the sweep and check the map for dark patches that remain; land travel alone leaves the far corners fogged.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang — all 9 gangs, as the PSN count records (Exophase, PSNProfiles). One operation per gang, not nine operations from one gang.

steps.t: Find an illegal operation run by each of the 9 gangs across Leonida.
Rob one operation per gang; the tracker below counts 9, one tick per gang.
Keep a note of which gangs you have hit — the count only finishes when every gang has lost one operation.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. A quiet moment trophy: go to a bar on Ocean Beach, order a cocktail, and take in the view — the location and the drink are both part of it.

steps.t: Go to Ocean Beach, the beachfront of Vice City shown in Rockstar's trailers.
Find a spot with a view over the beach and order a cocktail there.
Stay with the view until the trophy pops — it is a moment trophy, not a timed one.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. Drive a showroom car straight through the glass — the classic GTA way out of a car dealership, done on purpose this time.

steps.t: Go to a vehicle showroom in Leonida.
Get into a showroom vehicle and drive it out through the front of the showroom — smashing your way out is the condition, not buying the car.
Expect heat afterwards; have an escape in mind before you put your foot down.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley. Go bowling at that named alley and play the game through — the follow-through in the description is the point: finish the game, don't just throw one ball.

steps.t: Go to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley in Leonida.
Play a game of bowling there and follow through to its end.
Bowling also counts as one of the nine activity types for Master of None.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: A partnership with mass appeal. This hidden trophy's description is deliberately vague, and no published guide gives a confirmed trigger yet — it is tied to a partnership moment, most plausibly a co-op activity with your partner that draws a crowd.

steps.t: Play partner activities together as the story offers them; the trophy is listed as hidden, so its trigger is a story or partner moment, not a grind.
Treat any public-facing partner moment — a performance, a stunt, a showpiece — as a candidate trigger and check the trophy list after it.
This is the least certain trophy in the list: this guide marks it unconfirmed rather than inventing a trigger, and it will be corrected as players confirm it.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Choices made, for better or worse — and PSN tracks a count of 500 behind this trophy (Exophase, PSNProfiles). Keep making choices across the game and the count climbs; it is a long-haul tracker, not a single decision.

steps.t: Make choices whenever the game offers them — dialogue and action choices alike feed the count.
PSN records a count of 500 for this trophy, per Exophase and PSNProfiles — treat 500 choices as the target and use the tracker below.
Do not save-scum a single choice: the count rewards choices made across the whole game, not one repeated decision.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Second time's the charm. Fail at something, then succeed on the very next try — the trophy is for the comeback, so the failed first attempt is part of the recipe.

steps.t: Attempt something that can fail — a challenge, a stunt or a mission step — and fail it once.
Retry immediately and succeed on the second attempt; the trophy is for succeeding second time round.
If it does not pop, try a different activity: the trigger is a second-try success, and different activities all offer one.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: What the hell just happened? A hidden trophy for a strange encounter — the kind of odd, unexplained moment GTA hides in the corners of its map. Explore the weird places and the trophy finds you.

steps.t: Explore Leonida's odd corners — remote spots, strange landmarks and places that feel out of place.
Investigate anything strange you find rather than driving past it; the trophy's description is the game's own reaction to the encounter.
This trigger is unconfirmed in the published guides, so this guide marks it as such instead of inventing a location.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by. Drive past a target and knock them down with a melee attack from the moving vehicle — a drive-by with a bat, not a gun.

steps.t: Get a melee weapon and a vehicle, then find a target on foot.
Drive past and strike with the melee weapon from the moving vehicle — the knockdown, not the drive itself, is the condition.
The bowling alley from Let's Go Bowling is a fitting place to try it, but any on-foot target works.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills come from robberies and heists; your contacts clean them, and the cleaned total is what counts — $250,000 of it.

steps.t: Collect Marked Bills from robberies and heists — they are the dirty money the trophy is about.
Launder them through your contacts; fences become available gradually, per PowerPyx, and new ones unlock as you progress.
Keep laundering until $250,000 is cleaned in total; the tracker below counts to 250,000.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. Every shop counts toward one total — clothes, weapons, food, cars — so normal spending across a full playthrough gets most of the way there.

steps.t: Spend money in shops across Leonida; all shops feed the same $100,000 total.
Buy what you actually need first — gear, ammo and vehicles — and the total climbs without waste.
If you are short near the end, top up with big purchases such as vehicles; the tracker below counts to 100,000.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all garage properties — all 8, as the PSN count records (Exophase, PSNProfiles). Garages are property purchases, so this one costs money: save up, then buy the set.

steps.t: Find the garage properties for sale across Leonida; there are 8 to buy.
Buy all 8 garages — the trophy pops with the last purchase, not the first.
Fund them from heist and laundering income; Dime on the Dollar's $250,000 of cleaned money is the same cash flow.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. The app is the game's vehicle service: register ten different vehicles with it and the trophy pops.

steps.t: Open the Scooter Bros app and register a vehicle to it.
Register 10 vehicles in total; the tracker below counts to 10.
Vehicles you scan for Whip It Good are good candidates — scan first, then register.
